title: Modernize async pipeline with token-aware priority allocator and sliding-retry window
creator: Liam O'Connor
description:
Background: Our current async workers (Redis-backed leases and Kafka consumers) use coarse-grained concurrency controls and FIFO scheduling which leads to head-of-line blocking for long-running token-heavy requests. This manifests as elevated tail latency and less predictable throughput for mixed workloads (short chat responses vs. long-completion batches). We also have brittle retry semantics that occasionally amplify thundering retries after transient infra blips.

Goal: Replace the FIFO-first approach with a token-aware priority allocator that schedules work by estimated token cost and request priority, and add a sliding-retry window that spaces repeated attempts across time to avoid retry storms. The refactor should preserve semantics (at-least-once delivery where required), improve p95/p99 latency for short requests by 30% in mixed workloads, and reduce retry amplification incidents by 80%.

Success criteria:
- p95 for short requests (<=32 tokens) decreases by at least 30% under 50/50 mixed workload tests.
- Overall system throughput (tokens/sec) remains within 10% of current baseline for steady-state loads.
- Retry amplification incidents (post-mitigation incident counts) drop by >=80% in controlled chaos tests.
- No data loss; message delivery semantics maintained for critical topics.

Constraints and non-goals:
- We will not change persistence semantics of Redis streams or Kafka topics; offsets/acks behavior must remain compatible.
- This ticket is a refactor/tech-debt item and should avoid large API surface changes to callers.
- Deep vectorized kernel optimization is out-of-scope; focus is on orchestration and scheduling.

Design summary:
1) Token estimator: lightweight estimator runs at ingress to add estimated_token_count metadata based on model_id and requested max_tokens + prompt heuristics. estimator lives in the async ingress shim.
2) Priority allocator: worker-side allocator uses a multi-queue with buckets by (priority, token_range). Short token requests get a fast-path queue with preemptive slots; long requests go to background queues with limited concurrency. Tickets are scheduled by tokens-per-slot to equalize execution time share rather than request count.
3) Sliding-retry window: for retries we introduce partially-randomized backoff windows anchored to a per-tenant jitter seed and a global sliding window to avoid synchronized retries. Retries are queued in a rate-limited retry-executor with token-aware concurrency limits.
4) Lease-safe preemption: implement a lease-handoff protocol so long-running tasks can be paused (KV cache preserved for resumption) when preempted for high-priority short jobs.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): deploy token estimator and passive queue metrics (no scheduling changes) to gather distribution. (1 week)
- Phase 2 (soft-launch): enable token-aware allocation on 10% of ingress shards with aggressive telemetry. Monitor p95/p99, drops, and consumer lag. (2 weeks)
- Phase 3 (wide): progressively increase to 50% then 100% after stabilization, enable sliding-retry windows across consumers. (2–4 weeks)
- Fallback: toggle to legacy FIFO allocator via runtime feature flag and immediate circuit-breaker if errors > threshold.

Metrics and dashboards to add:
- per-queue p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens-per-second, queue-depth by token_range
- retry rate broken down by error class and tenant; inter-retry spacing histogram
- incident triggers: consumer error rate > 1% for 5min, unexpected offset seeks, lease transfer failures

Test plan:
- Unit tests for estimator and allocator logic, determinism for seeded jitter
- Integration: local harness with Redis streams + Kafka topics using synthetic mixed workloads
- Chaos testing: introduce transient Redis/Kafka failures and verify retry spacing prevents amplification
- Load tests: mixed job mix to validate p95 improvements and throughput constraints

Migration and compatibility:
- Legacy messages without estimated_token_count will default to conservative estimate fallback and land in medium bucket
- Schema version field added to message metadata; consumers tolerate unknown fields

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: estimator mis-predicts heavy tail requests; mitigation: fallback to legacy queue for requests that exceed measured runtime threshold and auto-learn estimator correction factors.
- Risk: lease-handoff complexity could increase failure modes; mitigation: start with cooperative pause (soft stop) before implementing full stateful handoff.

Open decisions:
- Whether to make token estimator model-specific rules or a trained lightweight predictor (we'll start rules-based).
- Lease handoff: two-step (soft pause -> resume) vs. full KV snapshot and restore; prefer soft pause for initial rollout.

- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Token-aware+Allocator+Design
- GH draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-runtime/pull/1298
- Load test harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/load-tests/tree/token-allocator
comments: 2026-02-14: Kickoff sync — aligned with Platform and Runtime teams on goals. Action: Ava to prototype estimator and queue metrics (Ava).

2026-02-20: Prototype completed — estimator added to ingress shim and emits estimated_token_count header (PR in draft, see PR 1298). Initial distribution shows long-tail for model-x. Noted need to cap conservative estimates to avoid starving background queue.

2026-02-26: Design review with SRE — agreed on sliding-retry parameters, added tenant-jitter seed to prevent cross-tenant synchronization. SRE requested additional monitoring for lease-handoff failures.

2026-03-03: Implementation update — allocator implemented behind feature flag; canary scheduled for Friday. Integration tests added for cooperative pause + resume. Review feedback: extract retry jitter into shared util and add deterministic unit tests (addressing in next PR).
2026-03-09: Canary deployed to 10% ingress shards. Early metrics: p95 for short jobs down ~22% (pre-tuning). Observed 3 lease-transfer timeouts — increasing soft-pause grace window to 2s.
